nodes.label: Brand Personality: Industrial, Exact, Unfussy
nodes.rationale: Three-word brand direction: industrial (not cute), exact (not approximate), unfussy (not stark). Chosen to match ops-tool audience who get dirt on their boots — no mascots, no celebration confetti.

nodes.label: Design Principles (5 rules)
nodes.rationale: Board is product; state is sacred; density with rhythm; action over chrome; quiet until something matters. Each principle derives from the dispatcher's real-time operational context.

nodes.label: Dry Hire Rental Paradigm
nodes.source_location: ### Fleet Rental Paradigms and Financial Modeling
nodes.rationale: Locks physical machinery only; client provides operator; fixed daily/weekly rate. Structurally decoupled from Wet Hire for accurate quoting and resource locking.

nodes.label: Wet Hire Rental Paradigm
nodes.source_location: ### Fleet Rental Paradigms and Financial Modeling
nodes.rationale: Locks machinery AND certified human operator; provider retains risk and compliance; combined hourly rate. Requires dual-resource lock and operator certification verification.

nodes.label: VMRS — Vehicle Maintenance Reporting Standards
nodes.source_location: ### Standard Repair Times and VMRS Integration
nodes.rationale: Nine-digit ATA coding standard mapped to Standard Repair Times (SRT) so dispatch durations are algorithmically derived, not guessed. Vehicle Difficulty Factor applied as multiplier.

nodes.label: OptaPlanner / Timefold AI Scheduling Solver
nodes.rationale: Solves VRPTW + Multi-skill Task Assignment via metaheuristics (Tabu Search, Simulated Annealing). Hard constraints prevent illegal assignments; soft constraints minimize travel and balance load. Shadow Variables cascade arrival times.

nodes.label: MQTT Broker (Field Telemetry Protocol)
nodes.source_location: ### Real-Time Network Protocols: MQTT vs. WebSockets
nodes.rationale: Chosen over WebSockets for mobile-to-backend because of broker-centric pub/sub, QoS levels (0/1/2), and resilience on intermittent cellular. WebSockets remain optimal for browser dashboard.

nodes.label: Flutter Mobile App (Mechanic Field App)
nodes.rationale: Dart cross-platform for iOS and Android. Adaptive GPS polling: high rate when EN_ROUTE, low rate when IN_PROGRESS. Clean Architecture + GetX state management + Hive offline cache.

nodes.label: PostGIS Spatial Database (ST_Point, KNN queries)
nodes.source_location: ## Backend Architecture: Java, Quarkus, and Vert.x
nodes.rationale: Complex geo queries at DB level not app memory. Geofences, KNN mechanic proximity, ST_Point for mechanic and vehicle locations. GIST index for <-> operator.

nodes.label: Design System: Precision Industrial / Dispatcher Console
nodes.norm_label: design system: precision industrial / dispatcher console

nodes.label: Color Palette: Warm Neutrals + Clay Accent + Semantic State Colors
nodes.rationale: Shifted away from cobalt-on-slate (read as generic-SaaS or SRE). Warm tinted neutrals hue 60-80 with clay accent at hue 38. State hues 25/82/150/230/295 spaced to survive colorblind grayscale. OKLCH throughout for perceptual uniformity.
nodes.norm_label: color palette: warm neutrals + clay accent + semantic state colors

nodes.label: Semantic State Color Pairs (enum-to-swatch mapping)
nodes.rationale: Same enum value always uses the same bg+fg pair across every surface. State-Is-Sacred rule: edit styles.css, never inline a one-off. Pairs: warn-amber REQUESTED/RESERVED, violet QUOTED, moss APPROVED/IN_PROGRESS, sky DISPATCHED/IDLE, neutral COMPLETED, brick CANCELLED.

nodes.label: Typography: Single System Sans Stack + Mono for Codes
nodes.rationale: One-Family Rule: no display face, hierarchy via weight (400/500/600) and scale. Mono stack reserved as vocabulary signal for serial numbers, VMRS codes, IDs, timestamps — not decorative.
nodes.norm_label: typography: single system sans stack + mono for codes

nodes.label: Elevation: Flat by Default (single modal lift only)
nodes.rationale: Flat-By-Default Rule. Only the modal sheet gets a box-shadow. Cards, panels, drawers separated by 1px hairline borders. Hover communicated by background tint not elevation.
nodes.norm_label: elevation: flat by default (single modal lift only)

nodes.label: Component Library: Buttons, Chips, Badges, Panels, Tables, Dispatch Timeline
nodes.norm_label: component library: buttons, chips, badges, panels, tables, dispatch timeline

nodes.label: Dispatch Timeline Component (.timeline)
nodes.rationale: State-driven event backgrounds via semantic pairs. Absence events at 0.78 opacity with 135deg repeating linear gradient so they read as unavailable. Today marker clay-soft tint. RBC content uses minmax(0,1fr) to prevent viewport overflow.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md — Claude Coding Guide for TerraPulse
nodes.norm_label: claude.md — claude coding guide for terrapulse

nodes.label: Stack Quirk: WS Broadcast via OpenConnections.listAll()
nodes.rationale: findByEndpointId() is not in the public 3.20 API; OpenConnections.listAll() is the correct broadcast pattern.
nodes.norm_label: stack quirk: ws broadcast via openconnections.listall()

nodes.label: Stack Quirk: Postgres NULL Named Parameter Type Inference
nodes.rationale: Named parameter with NULL value fails Postgres type inference — branch SQL instead (see MechanicRepository.findNearest).
nodes.norm_label: stack quirk: postgres null named parameter type inference

nodes.label: Stack Quirk: Custom DispatchGantt (not react-big-calendar)
nodes.rationale: RBC resource view puts resources as columns, not rows. Dispatch board needs mechanic rows × time columns (Gantt style), so a custom DispatchGantt was built. RBC is still used by AbsenceCalendarPicker.

nodes.label: Stack Quirk: @dnd-kit/core Drag Kinds (pool/event/resize)
nodes.rationale: Three drag kinds discriminated via DragStartEvent.active.data.current.kind: pool (unassigned card → POST schedule), event (existing block reassign/reschedule → PATCH schedule), resize (right-edge handle → PATCH schedule with updated scheduledEndAt). rowRefs Map used to convert cursor position to wall-clock time.

nodes.label: Architecture: Backend Layers (REST → Services → Repositories → Hibernate → PostGIS)
nodes.norm_label: architecture: backend layers (rest → services → repositories → hibernate → postgis)

nodes.label: Architecture Key Decisions
nodes.rationale: Reactive Quarkus+Vert.x for WS broadcast on event loop while REST stays on worker threads. PostGIS for geo (not in-memory). State machine guards in code not DB. Flyway owns DDL (Hibernate validate). WS broadcast via DispatchEventBus + OpenConnections.listAll(). React-query coarse keys invalidated by WS events.

nodes.label: Override Semantics (admin bypass: CANCELLED / REQUESTED hard reopen)
nodes.rationale: Override bypasses all guards. CANCELLED keeps history. REQUESTED is hard reopen: clears mechanic + lifecycle timestamps + actual_minutes. Every override appends audit line to notes. Emits SERVICE_ORDER_STATE_CHANGED with override=true.
nodes.norm_label: override semantics (admin bypass: cancelled / requested hard reopen)

nodes.label: Non-negotiable: Java 25 + Quarkus 3.31
nodes.rationale: Java 25 required; Quarkus 3.31 adds full Java 25 runtime + native image support. Older 3.20 needed Java 21 (Byte Buddy rejected JDK 25). .sdkmanrc pins 25.0.2-zulu.

nodes.label: Non-negotiable: Flyway Owns DDL (Hibernate validate only)
nodes.rationale: quarkus.hibernate-orm.database.generation=validate. Never let Hibernate auto-DDL. Migrations under backend/src/main/resources/db/migration/V*.sql.
nodes.norm_label: non-negotiable: flyway owns ddl (hibernate validate only)

nodes.label: Non-negotiable: State Machine Guards in ServiceOrderStateMachine
nodes.rationale: ServiceOrderStateMachine is source of truth for transitions. SCHEDULED requires non-null mechanic, start+end, non-overlapping window. Override endpoint is the only bypass (CANCELLED/REQUESTED targets only).
nodes.norm_label: non-negotiable: state machine guards in serviceorderstatemachine

nodes.label: Non-negotiable: DevResource gated by @IfBuildProfile(dev)
nodes.rationale: /api/dev/* only accessible in dev profile. Do not call from prod-style code paths.

nodes.label: Non-negotiable: Client FK Rules (Reservation NOT NULL, ServiceOrder nullable)
nodes.rationale: Reservation.client_id is NOT NULL — creating without clientId returns 400. ServiceOrder.client_id is nullable but UI's order-creation form requires it.
nodes.norm_label: non-negotiable: client fk rules (reservation not null, serviceorder nullable)

nodes.label: Java 25 Requirement
nodes.rationale: Quarkus 3.31 (Nov 2025) added full Java 25 support including native image builds with Mandrel. Earlier Quarkus 3.20 was stuck on Java 21 because Byte Buddy rejected JDK 25 class files. The repo pins 25.0.2-zulu via backend/.sdkmanrc. Java 21 still works with Quarkus 3.31 but is no longer required.

nodes.label: Precision Industrial Color Palette (warm off-white + industrial amber)
nodes.rationale: Warm off-white (#F8F7F4) avoids harshness of pure white for long shifts; industrial amber (#D97706) is high-visibility for primary actions and critical warnings; borders (#E5E7EB) used for structural definition in lieu of shadows to maintain flat industrial aesthetic.
nodes.norm_label: precision industrial color palette (warm off-white + industrial amber)

nodes.label: Precision Industrial Typography Strategy (Inter + JetBrains Mono)
nodes.rationale: Inter for all UI labels/headings (modern neutral, readable at small sizes). JetBrains Mono exclusively for data values, serial numbers, timestamps, coordinates — monospaced ensures numeric columns align perfectly for visual anomaly scanning in telemetry streams.
nodes.norm_label: precision industrial typography strategy (inter + jetbrains mono)

nodes.label: Industrial Minimalism Flat Design Principle
nodes.rationale: Hierarchy established through tonal layers and low-contrast outlines rather than shadows. Evokes high-end physical control panel: exact, unfussy, reliable. Designed for engineers and operators requiring clear data visualization under varying lighting conditions.

nodes.label: Industrial Telemetry Dark Color Palette (Deep Charcoal + Safety Orange)
nodes.rationale: Deep Charcoal (#1A1C1E) foundation provides blacked-out dashboard feel ensuring vibrant status colors pop without visual fatigue. Safety Orange (#F97316) reserved for CTAs, active alerts, critical navigation — mimics high-visibility gear on industrial sites. Reduces eye strain during long shifts.
nodes.norm_label: industrial telemetry dark color palette (deep charcoal + safety orange)

nodes.label: Industrial Telemetry Dual-Font Strategy
nodes.rationale: Inter for interface labels/headlines (legible at small scales, neutral professional tone). JetBrains Mono for hard data: VIN numbers, GPS coordinates, timestamps, fleet IDs — monospaced columns prevent errors reading similar chars like 0 and O. High-density logic with tight line heights.

nodes.label: High Density Maximum Context Layout Philosophy
nodes.rationale: 12-column fluid grid for desktop, 12px gutters for tight packing, 24px page margins to maximize internal real estate for maps and data tables. Compact vertical rhythm: 4px between related data points, 12-16px between functional groups. Mobile collapses to single column with horizontal scrolling rather than hiding columns.
nodes.norm_label: high density maximum context layout philosophy

nodes.label: Flutter Mechanic App (Deferred for POC)
nodes.rationale: Flutter mechanic app deferred for POC. Target architecture includes Flutter + flutter_foreground_task + geolocator + MQTT per Pre plan prompt 1.md. GPS updates simulated via backend dev-only endpoint POST /api/dev/simulate-move.
